name: lr_message
description: Sends a message to the log file and the output window (output.txt when run in VuGen). Logging must be enabled in Runtime Settings with the "Always send messages" option. Returns the message length, or a negative number on failure.

args.name: format
args.desc: printf-style format string.

args.name: exp1, exp2,..expn
args.desc: Expressions/variables to format and print.

name: lr_next_row
description: Advances to the next row in a parameter data file (.dat); if already on the last row, wraps back to the first row. Most useful for Table-type parameters because all parameters in the file advance together. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: dat_file
args.desc: Name of the parameter .dat file that contains the values to retrieve.

name: lr_output_message
description: Sends a message to the log file, the output window, and the test report summary, together with the script section name and line number. The message is always shown in the output window regardless of the logging settings, and is truncated if it exceeds 5 KB. Returns the message length, or a negative number on failure.

args.name: format
args.desc: printf-style format string.

args.name: exp1, exp2,..expn
args.desc: Expressions/variables to format and print.

example: lr_output_message( "We are on iteration #%s", lr_eval_string( "{iteration}" ) );

name: lr_param_increment
description: Takes the value of source_param, increments it by one, and stores the result as a null-terminated string in destination_param. The source value must be an integer (single-byte digits with an optional sign); if destination_param already exists, its value is overwritten. Returns 0 on success and a negative number for various failures.

args.name: destination_param
args.desc: Destination parameter that stores the incremented result.

args.name: source_param
args.desc: Source parameter whose value is incremented by one.

name: lr_param_sprintf
signature: int lr_param_sprintf( const char *paramName, const char * format [,args_... ] );
description: Writes formatted output to a parameter, similar to C sprintf but with a parameter as the destination instead of a buffer. Some format specifiers are not supported (for example %E, %hd, %lld). Returns 0 on success and a non-zero value on failure.

args.name: paramName
args.desc: Destination parameter to which the string is written.

args.name: format
args.desc: Format string (format characters).

args.name: args
args.desc: Optional print arguments.

name: lr_param_unique
description: Creates a unique string in the format <GroupName><UserID><CurrentTime> (no spaces) and stores it in a parameter. Returns 0 on success and a non-zero value on failure.

args.name: paramName
args.desc: Destination parameter to which the unique string is written.

name: lr_paramarr_idx
signature: char * lr_paramarr_idx( const char * paramArrayName, unsigned int index);
description: Returns the parameter value at a given position in a parameter array (one-based index). If the parameter does not exist, returns the string "{paramArrayName_index}"; on error returns NULL. Memory is allocated internally and freed automatically at the end of each iteration.

args.name: paramArrayName
args.desc: Name of the parameter array from which the value is retrieved.

args.name: index
args.desc: Position of the parameter in the array (one-based).

name: lr_paramarr_len
description: Returns the number of elements in a parameter array. Returns -1 on error and 0 if the parameter is not an array.

args.name: paramArrayName
args.desc: Name of the parameter array.

name: lr_paramarr_random
description: Returns the parameter value at a random position in a parameter array. Returns a pointer to a string buffer containing that value, or NULL if the array is empty or does not exist. Standard parameterization is not available for this function.

args.name: paramArrayName
args.desc: Name of the parameter array from which a random value is retrieved.

name: lr_peek_events
description: Pauses Vuser script execution and checks for events before continuing. C-language scripts perform this check automatically, so an explicit call is not needed (it is required in Java scripts). Returns no value.

name: lr_read_file
signature: int lr_read_file( const char *filename_, const char *outputParam_, int continueOnError_ );
description: Reads the contents of a file and stores them in a parameter. Returns the number of bytes read, or a negative number on failure.

args.name: filename
args.desc: Full path of the file, or a path relative to the script folder.

args.name: outputParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the file contents.

args.name: continueOnError
args.desc: LR_EXIT_VUSER (0) or LR_EXIT_ACTION_AND_CONTINUE (1).

name: lr_remove_custom_error_message
description: Removes the custom error text previously set with lr_set_custom_error_message. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

name: lr_rendezvous
description: Creates a rendezvous point in a Vuser script: when executed, the Vuser stops and waits for permission to continue. Works only in the action section (not init/end) and always returns zero.

args.name: rendezvous_name
args.desc: Rendezvous name.

name: lr_rendezvous_ex
description: Creates a rendezvous point; the Vuser stops and waits for permission to continue (default timeout of 30 seconds from the scenario policy in the Controller). Unlike lr_rendezvous, this function returns a status such as LR_REND_ALL_ARRIVED (0), LR_REND_TIMEOUT (1), LR_REND_DISABLED (2), and others.

args.name: rendezvous_name
args.desc: Rendezvous name.

name: lr_resume_transaction
description: Resumes reporting of transaction data that was previously frozen by lr_stop_transaction. After resuming, the transaction "get" functions return all data accumulated since the transaction started, including the period during which it was stopped. Returns no value.

args.name: transaction_name
args.desc: Name of the transaction to resume.

name: lr_resume_transaction_instance
description: Resumes reporting of transaction instance data that was previously stopped with lr_stop_transaction_instance. Data collection continues while stopped; only the reporting is frozen. Returns no value.

args.name: trans_handle
args.desc: Transaction instance ID returned by lr_start_transaction_instance.

name: lr_save_datetime
signature: void lr_save_datetime( const char *format, int offset, const char *name );
description: Saves the current date and time (or a date and time with a given offset) to a parameter. The result is truncated if it exceeds MAX_DATETIME_LEN characters. The format can use built-in constants (lrun.h) or custom format codes. Returns no value.

args.name: format
args.desc: Format of the date/time information to save.

args.name: offset
args.desc: Offset from the current time: DATE_NOW, TIME_NOW, ONE_DAY, ONE_HOUR, ONE_MIN.

args.name: name
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the date/time.

name: lr_save_int
signature: int lr_save_int( int value, const char *param_name);
description: Converts an integer to a string and stores it in a parameter; the parameter is created if it does not exist. Returns LR_PASS on success and a negative value on failure.

args.name: value
args.desc: Integer value to assign to the parameter.

args.name: param_name
args.desc: Parameter name.

name: lr_save_param_regexp
signature: int lr_save_param_regexp (char* bufferToSearch, int bufferSize, char * RegExp[/IC], int Ordinal, char * ResultParam, LAST);
description: Searches a buffer for regular expression matches and stores the matching capture group in a parameter or parameter array. The regex must have exactly one capture group; Ordinal=All fills the array. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: bufferToSearch
args.desc: Buffer to search (may contain binary data).

args.name: bufferSize
args.desc: Buffer size in bytes.

args.name: RegExp[/IC]
args.desc: Regular expression with one capture group; the /IC suffix makes it case-insensitive.

args.name: Ordinal
args.desc: Match ordinal (one-based); 0 or All for all matches; default 1.

args.name: ResultParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the result.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_save_searched_string
signature: int lr_save_searched_string( char *buffer, long buf_size, unsigned int occurrence, char *search_string, int offset, unsigned int string_len, char *parm_name );
description: Searches a buffer for an occurrence of a string and saves part of the buffer that follows that string to a parameter. The occurrence argument is zero-based.

args.name: buffer
args.desc: STRING or CARRAY buffer to search.

args.name: buf_size
args.desc: Buffer size.

args.name: occurrence
args.desc: Occurrence number of search_string (starting at 0).

args.name: search_string
args.desc: String to search for in the buffer.

args.name: offset
args.desc: Number of characters to skip after the end of the search_string occurrence.

args.name: string_len
args.desc: Number of characters to save.

args.name: parm_name
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the result.

example:
char cBuff[] = "abc Emma Woodhouse abc Elizabeth Bennet abc William Price";
lr_save_searched_string(cBuff, strlen(cBuff),
2, "abc",// Search for third occurrence of "abc"
1,       // Skip the space after "abc"
4,       // Put the next four characters...
"Fannys_brother"); // ... in parameter Fannys_brother.

name: lr_save_string
signature: int lr_save_string( const char *param_value, const char *param_name);
description: Saves a null-terminated string to a parameter; useful for correlation. Retrieve the value again with lr_eval_string. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: param_value
args.desc: Value to assign to the parameter.

args.name: param_name
args.desc: Parameter name (case-sensitive).

name: lr_save_timestamp
signature: int lr_save_timestamp( const char* tmstampParam, [DIGITS,] LAST );
description: Saves the current local timestamp of the machine running the script to a parameter (not as an integer). Defaults to 13 digits (epoch milliseconds); use DIGITS=10 for seconds. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success.

args.name: tmstampParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the timestamp.

args.name: DIGITS
args.desc: Optional: number of timestamp digits (default 13; values outside 1-16 are treated as 13).

name: lr_save_var
signature: int lr_save_var( char *param_value, unsigned long const value_len, unsigned long const options, char *param_name );
description: Assigns a string of a specified length to a parameter; useful for correlation. Do not save buffers containing nulls or binary data, and do not pass a value_len longer than the actual data. Returns 0 on success and 1 on failure.

args.name: param_value
args.desc: Value to assign to the parameter.

args.name: value_len
args.desc: Length of the value in bytes.

args.name: options
args.desc: Parameter options, currently 0.

args.name: param_name
args.desc: Parameter name.

name: lr_set_custom_error_message
signature: int lr_set_custom_error_message( const char *format, exp1, exp2,...expn. );
description: Sets custom text, in printf-style format, that is emitted after the built-in error message in the Output window. Cancel it with lr_remove_custom_error_message. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: format
args.desc: Format string for the Output window.

args.name: exp1, exp2,.. expn
args.desc: Expressions/variables to format.

name: lr_set_debug_message
signature: int lr_set_debug_message( unsigned int message_level_flag, unsigned int on_off );
description: Changes the message level (debug bitmap) during script execution, which determines the information sent by lr_message, lr_log_message, lr_output_message, and lr_debug_message. Cumulative: each call only turns the specified flags on or off. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: message_level_flag
args.desc: One of the Message Log flags in Runtime Settings (for example, LR_MSG_CLASS_EXTENDED_LOG).

args.name: on_off
args.desc: LR_SWITCH_ON or LR_SWITCH_OFF.

name: lr_set_transaction
signature: int lr_set_transaction(const char *name, double duration, int status);
description: Creates a complete transaction with its duration and status in a single call (created and closed immediately). Useful for non-sequential business processes or for summing the durations of several sets of steps. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: name
args.desc: Transaction name.

args.name: duration
args.desc: Transaction duration in seconds.

args.name: status
args.desc: Transaction status: LR_PASS, LR_FAIL, or LR_STOP (LR_AUTO is not valid).

example: lr_set_transaction("Multiple_Orders", 45.3, LR_PASS);

name: lr_set_transaction_instance_status
description: Sets the status of an open transaction instance, identified by the handle returned from lr_start_transaction_instance. lr_end_transaction_instance must use LR_AUTO for this status to take effect. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure.

args.name: status
args.desc: One of the transaction status constants: pass, fail, or stop (auto is not valid).

args.name: trans_handle
args.desc: Transaction instance handle.

name: lr_set_transaction_status
description: Sets the status of all open transactions whose lr_end_transaction uses LR_AUTO, overriding the default LR_PASS status. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure.

args.name: status
args.desc: One of the transaction status constants: pass, fail, or stop (auto is not valid).

name: lr_set_transaction_status_by_name
description: Sets the default status of an open transaction by name; that transaction's lr_end_transaction must use LR_AUTO. Returns 0 on success and a negative value on failure.

args.name: status
args.desc: One of the transaction status constants: pass, fail, or stop (auto is not valid).

args.name: trans_name
args.desc: Transaction name.

name: lr_start_cross_vuser_transaction
description: Starts a transaction that is ended by one or more other Vusers (not the starting Vuser). It is called by the Vuser that triggers the event, for example by sending a message. The receiving Vuser calls lr_end_cross_vuser_transaction. This function is not recorded and must be added manually. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: transaction_name
args.desc: Cross-Vuser transaction name.

args.name: trans_id_param
args.desc: Parameter containing the transaction ID string (also used by lr_end_cross_vuser_transaction).

name: lr_start_sub_transaction
description: Starts a sub-transaction under its parent transaction name, to break down part of a business process (for example, "electrical_purchases" within "purchases"). Each lr_start_sub_transaction must be paired with lr_end_sub_transaction. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the name is invalid or the parent is not found.

args.name: sub_transaction_
args.desc: Sub-transaction name.

args.name: parent_transaction_
args.desc: Name of the parent transaction that contains the sub-transaction.

name: lr_start_timer
description: Starts a timer that measures time in seconds (maximum resolution of microseconds). Returns a merc_timer_handle_t handle that you pass to lr_end_timer to stop the timer.

name: lr_start_transaction
description: Marks the beginning of a transaction; paired with lr_end_transaction for transaction analysis. Transactions can be nested, but every lr_start_transaction must have a matching lr_end_transaction. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the transaction name is invalid.

args.name: transaction_name
args.desc: Transaction name.

name: lr_start_transaction_instance
description: Marks the beginning of a transaction instance; multiple instances with the same name are distinguished by unique handles. Passing a parent transaction handle creates a sub-transaction instance, while 0 creates a new parent transaction. Returns the instance handle (long), or a negative number on error; must be paired with lr_end_transaction_instance.

args.name: transaction_name
args.desc: Transaction name.

args.name: handle
args.desc: Parent transaction handle; 0 to create a new parent transaction.

name: lr_stop_transaction
description: Freezes transaction data reporting: the transaction "get" functions reflect data only up to the point of the call until lr_resume_transaction is called. Provided for compatibility; newer alternatives are lr_start_sub_transaction and lr_set_transaction. Returns the transaction duration in milliseconds, or a negative number on error.

args.name: transaction_name
args.desc: Name of an open transaction started with lr_start_transaction.

name: lr_stop_transaction_instance
description: Freezes the reporting statistics of a transaction instance, identified by its handle, until lr_resume_transaction_instance is called; data collection continues in the background. Returns the current duration of the transaction instance in seconds, or a negative number on error.

args.name: parent_handle
args.desc: Unique transaction instance handle returned by lr_start_transaction_instance.

name: lr_think_time
description: Pauses execution between commands in a script to simulate user think time. With cross-step downloads or asynchronous functions, a long think time can cause downloads to time out. Does not return a value.

args.name: thinkTime
args.desc: Pause duration in seconds.

name: lr_unmask
description: Generated during recording to encode passwords: VuGen records the actual password but displays an encoded version inside lr_unmask, and this function decodes it during replay. Returns a pointer to the decoded string, or NULL on error.

args.name: EncodedString
args.desc: Encoded string to unmask.

example:
edit_set("FNDSCSGN.SIGNON.USERNAME.0", "OPERATIONS");
edit_set("FNDSCSGN.SIGNON.PASSWORD.0",lr_unmask("38620da61ca1093e7aa7ec"));

name: lr_unzip
description: Decompresses the contents of a parameter and saves the result to another parameter. Returns LR_PASS on success, or LR_FAIL if the source parameter does not exist or decompression fails.

args.name: source
args.desc: Parameter containing the compressed data.

args.name: target
args.desc: Destination parameter for the decompressed result.

name: lr_user_data_point
description: Records a user-defined data sample for analysis; the sample time is recorded automatically and the results appear in the User Defined Data Points graph. The prefixes HTTP, NON_HTTP, RETRY, mic_, stream_, and mms_ (case-sensitive) are reserved. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the write fails.

args.name: sample_name
args.desc: Data point name.

args.name: value
args.desc: Value to record.

name: lr_user_data_point_ex
signature: int lr_user_data_point_ex( const char *sample_name, double value, int log_flag );
description: Same as lr_user_data_point, with an additional log_flag argument that controls whether the data point is written to the Vuser log (output.txt in VuGen), depending on the runtime log settings. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the write fails.

args.name: sample_name
args.desc: Sample type name.

args.name: value
args.desc: Value to record.

args.name: log_flag
args.desc: DP_FLAGS_NO_LOG (1), DP_FLAGS_STANDARD_LOG (2), or DP_FLAGS_EXTENDED_LOG (3).

name: lr_user_data_point_instance
signature: long lr_user_data_point_instance( char *sample_name, double value, long transaction_handle );
description: Records a user-defined data sample and correlates it with a transaction instance, for applications integrated with OpenText Professional Performance Engineering. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the write fails.

args.name: sample_name
args.desc: Sample type name.

args.name: value
args.desc: Value to record.

args.name: transaction_handle
args.desc: Identifier of the transaction instance associated with the data point.

name: lr_user_data_point_instance_ex
signature: long lr_user_data_point_instance_ex(const char* sample_name, double value, long transaction_handle, int log_flag);
description: Same as lr_user_data_point_instance, with an additional log_flag that controls whether the data point is written to the Vuser log, according to the runtime log settings. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the write fails.

args.name: sample_name
args.desc: Sample type name.

args.name: value
args.desc: Value to record.

args.name: transaction_handle
args.desc: Identifier of the associated transaction instance.

args.name: log_flag
args.desc: DP_FLAGS_NO_LOG (1), DP_FLAGS_STANDARD_LOG, or DP_FLAGS_EXTENDED_LOG (3).

name: lr_vuser_status_message
description: Sends a string to the Status area in the Controller and to the Vuser log (output.txt when run in VuGen). Returns the length of the message sent on success, or a negative number on failure.

args.name: format
args.desc: printf-style format string.

args.name: exp1, exp2,..expn
args.desc: Expressions/variables to format and print.

example: lr_vuser_status_message( "We are on iteration #%s", lr_eval_string( "{iteration}" ) );

name: lr_wasted_time
description: Subtracts time wasted on incidental/secondary actions from all currently open transactions. The value is given in milliseconds. Does not return a value.

args.name: wasteTime
args.desc: Wasted time (long, in milliseconds) to subtract from open transactions.

name: lr_whoami
description: Returns information about the Vuser running the script: the Vuser ID, Vuser group name, and scenario ID. Memory for the sgroup string is allocated automatically; unneeded arguments can be replaced with NULL. The scenario ID is 0 if the scenario attribute has not been added in Runtime Settings.

args.name: vuser_id
args.desc: Output: Vuser ID number.

args.name: sgroup
args.desc: Output: Vuser group name.

args.name: scid
args.desc: Output: scenario/session ID.

name: lr_xml_delete
signature: int lr_xml_delete( <List of specifications> [, <List of optional specifications> ] [, LAST]);
description: Queries the input XML string and deletes the matching fragments; the resulting XML is saved to the output parameter with the original encoding preserved. Elements left empty after deletion are written as self-closing tags (for example, <e/>).

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string to query.

args.name: ResultParam
args.desc: Output parameter for the resulting XML data.

args.name: Query
args.desc: XML query to run on the input string.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: yes: process all matches; no (default): first match only.

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Behavior when no match is found.

name: lr_xml_extract
signature: int lr_xml_extract( <List of specifications> [, <List of optional specifications> ] [, LAST]);
description: Queries the input XML string and extracts the matching fragments to the XMLFragmentParam output parameter.

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string to query.

args.name: XMLFragmentParam
args.desc: Output parameter for the extracted XML fragment.

args.name: Query
args.desc: XML query or Fast Query.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: yes: all matches; no (default): first match only.

args.name: ResolveNameSpaces
args.desc: yes: include full namespace prefix resolution; no (default).

args.name: OutputFormat
args.desc: utf-8 or locale (default).

name: lr_xml_find
signature: int lr_xml_find( <List of specifications> [, <List of optional specifications> ] [, LAST]);
description: Queries the input XML string for matching values and returns the number of matching occurrences (1 or 0 when SelectAll=no).

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string to query.

args.name: Query
args.desc: XML query or Fast Query.

args.name: Value / ValueParam
args.desc: String to search for (element or attribute value), given directly or through a parameter.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: yes: process all matches; no (default).

args.name: IgnoreCase
args.desc: yes: ignore case; no (default).

args.name: UseRegExp
args.desc: yes: use a regular expression; no (default).

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: continue or error when no match is found.

name: lr_xml_get_values
signature: int lr_xml_get_values( <List of specifications> [, <List of optional specifications> ] [, LAST]);
description: Queries the input XML string for values that match the Query criteria and saves the results to the output parameter.

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string to query.

args.name: ValueParam
args.desc: Output parameter that stores the query result.

args.name: Query
args.desc: XML query or Fast Query.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: yes: process all matches; no (default): first match only.

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Behavior when no match is found.

name: lr_xml_insert
signature: int lr_xml_insert( <List of specifications> [, <List of optional specifications> ] [, LAST]);
description: Queries the input XML string and inserts an XML fragment at the specified position; the result is saved to the output parameter with the original encoding preserved.

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string to query.

args.name: ResultParam
args.desc: Output parameter for the XML after insertion.

args.name: Query
args.desc: XML query to run on the input string.

args.name: XmlFragment
args.desc: String to insert (a new element or attribute).

args.name: XmlFragmentParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the string to insert.

args.name: Position
args.desc: before, after (default), child, or attribute.

name: lr_xml_replace
signature: int lr_xml_replace( <List of specifications> [, <List of optional specifications> ] [, LAST]);
description: Queries the input XML string and replaces the matching parts with a new value, either a literal string or a parameter. The resulting XML is saved to the output parameter with the original encoding preserved.

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string to query.

args.name: ResultParam
args.desc: Output parameter for the resulting XML.

args.name: Query
args.desc: XML query to run on the input.

args.name: XmlFragment
args.desc: Literal replacement string.

args.name: XmlFragmentParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the replacement value.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: yes: all matches; no (default): first match only.

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Behavior when no match is found.

name: lr_xml_set_values
signature: int lr_xml_set_values( <List of specifications> [, <List of optional specifications> ] [, LAST]);
description: Queries the input XML string and sets new values on the matching elements. If multiple values need to be replaced, store them in parameters named Param_1, Param_2, and so on. The original XML encoding is preserved.

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string to query.

args.name: ResultParam
args.desc: Output parameter containing the XML after the values are changed.

args.name: Query
args.desc: XML query (element or attribute).

args.name: Value
args.desc: String value to assign to the matching elements.

args.name: ValueParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the value to assign.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: yes: all matches; no (default): first match only.

name: lr_xml_transform
description: Applies an XSL (Extensible Stylesheet Language) transformation to the input XML data and saves the formatted result to the output parameter, preserving the original XML encoding.

args.name: XML
args.desc: Input XML string.

args.name: Stylesheet
args.desc: XSL specification in XSL string format.

args.name: ResultParam
args.desc: Output parameter containing the transformed data.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the specification list.

name: lr_zip
description: Compresses the contents of a parameter and saves the result to another parameter. Returns LR_PASS on success, or LR_FAIL if the source parameter does not exist or compression fails.

args.name: source
args.desc: Parameter containing the data to compress.

args.name: target
args.desc: Destination parameter for the compressed result.
